findings.issue: While the per-source refresh limit is active, refreshAfterSignatureMiss throws a plain Error even when the key set it just checked came from a forced refresh completed moments earlier. The only escape is `newer.version > initial.version`, and that check fails when `initial` is itself the freshly refreshed set. So after any bad-signature token forces a refresh at t0, every other definitively invalid optional bearer before t0+30s gets a 500 instead of public mode. Examples: a forged token, or a token signed by a key that has since been retired. A miss against a set fetched under 30 seconds ago is not ambiguous. docs/framework/contracts/tenancy-context-1.5.md only requires failure when 'no newly refreshed set can establish definitive rejection'. DETRAN UPS-TEN-03 (MUST under OD-S15-01) says 'inválido … → modo público'. Any anonymous caller can trigger this: sending one garbage token every 30 seconds keeps the window open. The test 'coalesces concurrent forced refreshes and suppresses another ambiguous refresh for 30 seconds' in packages/auth/test/unit/validators.spec.ts locks this in. Right after the coalesced refresh, it asserts that unknownToken rejects as a non-InvalidCredentialError at the same Date.now().
findings.required_change: Architect: state in the contract that a usable key set obtained by a forced refresh that started inside the current 30-second window can establish definitive rejection. Engineer: record on CachedKeySet whether it came from a forced refresh and when (e.g. `refreshedAt`). When a miss happens during suppression and the verifying set is a forced refresh from inside that window, throw InvalidCredentialError. Throw a non-InvalidCredentialError only if that set is older than the last forced refresh start or the refresh failed. Inspector: change the suppression test so a miss against the just-refreshed set is typed invalid. Add a case where a refresh failure inside the window, or a stale non-refreshed set during suppression, still rejects as non-InvalidCredentialError, with no nominal fallback. Architect: rebind law/trace.json and the API baseline if the declarations change.

findings.issue: The test titled 'refreshes a stale jwksUri cache once for a rotated valid token and propagates refresh failure' only covers two successful fetches. The jwksUri refresh-failure branch is never tested; only the signing-service refresh failure is. This test and 'treats malformed, empty, and unusable jwksUri responses…' also reassign global.fetch without try/finally, so an assertion failure leaks the mock into later tests.
findings.required_change: Inspector: add a jwksUri case where the forced re-fetch rejects or returns !ok after a cached set. Assert a non-InvalidCredentialError and that fetch was called exactly twice. Restore global.fetch in finally. Architect: rebind trace.

summary:
All cycle-3 findings except one are repaired and hold against the source. The JWKS refresh-suppression window adds a new MUST deviation, so the verdict is REVIEW.

(1) Interceptor order: the order test now reorders the real APP_INTERCEPTOR instances before app.init(). I checked this against @nestjs/core 11.2.3. APP_INTERCEPTOR instances are added to the shared ApplicationConfig by scanner.applyApplicationProviders() inside TestingModuleBuilder.compile(). getGlobalInterceptors() returns that live array, which the test splices in place. The router copies the list only during init(). The test wraps the instance-level intercept methods and resets and asserts the calls per request, for both orders on /order/protected and /order/public. It asserts the same generated UUIDv7 in the pre-interceptor guard, the handler and the response header. The CI log shows 2/2 passing.

(2) JWKS parsing and classification: decodeJwtClaims types syntax errors itself, and a non-RS256 alg is typed invalid before any key lookup. A missing, non-array, empty or all-unusable key set now throws a plain Error for both sources. A signature miss forces one resolveKeys(true), coalesced through inFlight per source. Real RSA/JOSE tests cover signing-service and jwksUri rotation, a real bad signature, signing-service refresh failure, coalescing and the 30-second limit. Issuer, audience, exp and nbf checks run only after a valid signature and do not trigger a refresh.

(3) Other cycle-3 items:
- Typed AuthContextGuard rejection gives 200 nominal; a generic error gives 500.
- A revoked STYNX session over HTTP gives an exact nominal body with no principal or session.
- Cognito JOSE codes are separated from JWKS timeout, no-matching-key and fetch failures.
- Both guards clear all fields plus both markers on the absent, typed-invalid and non-optional paths.
- An unmarked tenant-B claim under Host A gives 200 nominal.
- The backend-only principal gets an exact 403 from PermissionGuard.

(4) Baselines: record.md explains the flow.d.ts union-order digest. The emitted packages/auth/dist/auth/src/stynx-jwt.validator.d.ts hashes to 37c5d5d2…, matching the rebind in 3314eb69; it only adds private members.

Other checks:
- Commits are role-separated: Inspector changed tests only, Engineer changed src only, Architect changed docs, law and work.
- The fixed-group changeset is a minor bump.
- pnpm check:trace reports 393/393 at HEAD.
- The removed test lines only tighten assertions or follow the contract change on empty JWKS sets.
- No workflow, package.json or reference manifest was touched. No DETRAN code was copied.

Remaining gap: a definitively invalid optional bearer that arrives within 30 seconds of a forced refresh still gets a 500 instead of public mode. That contradicts UPS-TEN-03 and the contract's 'newly refreshed set' wording.
